theme: The Prophet ﷺ is not astray: what he brings is revelation he truly received. The idols are empty names, each soul answers for its own effort, and the Hour is near, so bow to Allah.
story: Revealed in Makkah, likely in the fifth year of prophethood. Until then the Prophet ﷺ had shared the Quran mostly in private. The Quraysh told people he had gone astray, and raised an uproar whenever he tried to recite it publicly.

It was the first surah revealed with a prostration. The Prophet ﷺ recited it publicly in Makkah, reportedly at the Kaʿbah, then prostrated, and believers and disbelievers alike prostrated with him. One old man, reportedly Umayyah ibn Khalaf, only lifted dust to his forehead, and later died a disbeliever.

News that Makkah had bowed reached the emigrants in Abyssinia, and some returned, only to find the hostility unchanged. Embarrassed, the Quraysh claimed they had heard him praise their goddesses, a claim that cannot fit a surah calling those goddesses empty names (23).

sections.title: The Prophet ﷺ isn’t astray: Jibrīl taught him; he saw great signs
sections.meaning: Allah swears by the setting star that the Prophet ﷺ has not strayed and speaks only revelation. A mighty angel, Jibrīl, taught him, appearing on the horizon and coming close. He saw him again at the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary, and truly saw his Lord’s greatest signs.
points: By the star: your companion hasn’t strayed; he speaks only revelation
Taught by one mighty in power, who came within two bow-lengths
His heart didn’t lie about what he saw; will you dispute it?
He saw him again at the Lote Tree, by the Garden of Refuge
His sight didn’t swerve; he saw his Lord’s greatest signs
sections.matters: Makkah said he had gone astray. The surah opens by answering that head-on: his message is not his own idea but revelation, delivered by a mighty, trustworthy angel he saw with his own eyes. Everything that follows rests on this.
sections.story: The Quraysh called the Prophet ﷺ misguided and said he made the Quran up himself. The first sighting was on the horizon, reportedly in Makkah; the second was at the Lote Tree during the Night Journey (Isrāʾ and Miʿrāj).
explained: Allah swears by the star as it sets. Ṣāḥibukum, “your companion”, reminds Makkah that they had known his honesty all his life. He has not strayed through ignorance or erred on purpose, and nothing he says comes from his own desire. It is waḥy: revelation, taught by Jibrīl, dhū mirrah, mighty and strong.

Jibrīl appeared in his true form on the high horizon, then came down within two bow-lengths or nearer. The Prophet ﷺ saw him again at Sidrat al-Muntahā, beside Paradise, as something indescribable covered the tree. His eyes neither wandered nor overstepped. Most reports say he saw Jibrīl both times; one view says he saw his Lord with his heart.
teaches: What the Prophet ﷺ taught came from Allah, not from his own desire.
Revelation came through a mighty, trustworthy angel, safe from any tampering.
Arguing about what you never saw is like the blind disputing with the sighted.
In Allah’s presence, keep your gaze where it belongs: don’t wander or overstep.
sections.hook: Hawā (1, the star falls) and al-hawā (3, desire) sound alike. Seeing repeats: raʾā (11), yarā (12), raʾāhu (13), raʾā (18). Awḥā … mā awḥā (10) matches yaghshā … mā yaghshā (16).

sections.title: Al-Lāt, al-ʿUzzā, Manāt are empty names; even angels need Allah’s permission
sections.meaning: Have you considered your idols al-Lāt, al-ʿUzzā and Manāt? You keep sons for yourselves and give Allah daughters, an unfair split. They are only names you and your fathers invented, followed on guesswork and desire. Man doesn’t get whatever he wishes; even the angels can intercede only with Allah’s permission.
points: Have you considered al-Lāt, al-ʿUzzā, and Manāt, the third?
Sons for you, daughters for Him? An unfair division
Mere names with no authority, followed on guesswork and desire
Man doesn’t get whatever he wishes; both lives belong to Allah
Even angels’ intercession helps only after Allah permits
sections.matters: After proving the Prophet ﷺ brings real revelation, the surah turns to what Makkah followed instead: invented names. It exposes their double standard and ends the hope that idols, or even angels, can win favour with Allah without His permission.
sections.story: The Arabs had many idols, but these three were the most famous: al-Lāt at Ṭāʾif, al-ʿUzzā at Nakhlah, Manāt at Qudayd. The pagans called the angels Allah’s daughters while disliking daughters themselves. All three idols were later destroyed.
explained: Al-Lāt, al-ʿUzzā and Manāt were the great idols of Arabia, with names reportedly taken from Allah’s own names. The pagans claimed Allah had daughters, yet were upset when a daughter was born to them. So Allah asks: sons for you and daughters for Him? That is qismah ḍīzā, a crooked, unjust division.

These gods are only names, with no proof from Allah, followed on ẓann (guesswork) and desire, though guidance had already come. Does man get whatever he wants? No: this life and the next belong to Allah. Even the honoured angels can’t intercede unless Allah permits and is pleased with the one they speak for.
teaches: Beliefs need proof from Allah, not inherited names or guesswork.
Don’t attribute to Allah what you would reject for yourself.
Wishing is not enough; this life and the next belong to Allah.
Intercession works only with Allah’s permission, for those He is pleased with.
sections.hook: The idols come in order: al-Lāt, al-ʿUzzā, then Manāt “the third”. Ayah 23 mirrors ayah 4: in huwa illā waḥy becomes in hiya illā asmāʾ, “only names”. The ۞ marks ayah 26.

sections.title: Calling angels female is guesswork; Allah rewards those who avoid major sins
sections.meaning: Those who deny the Hereafter give the angels female names, with no knowledge, only guesswork, and guesswork is no substitute for truth. So turn away from those who want only this world; that is the limit of their knowledge. Allah owns everything and will repay each. He forgives small slips, so don’t praise yourselves.
points: Deniers of the Hereafter name angels female; guesswork can’t replace truth
Turn from those who want only this world; Allah knows who is guided
Everything is Allah’s: evil repaid, good rewarded with the best
Avoid major sins; small slips are forgiven; don’t claim purity
sections.matters: It names the root of the problem: not believing in the Hereafter, so this world becomes the limit of what people know. Then it describes the good-doer realistically: not sinless, but avoiding major sins, relying on Allah’s vast forgiveness, and not praising himself.
sections.story: Ayah 29 is reportedly about an-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith or al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah. The end of 32 reportedly answered people who boasted, “our prayer, our fasting, our Hajj”. Other reports tie its mention of small slips to different occasions.
explained: Because they don’t believe in the Hereafter, they dare to call the angels Allah’s daughters. They have no knowledge, only ẓann, and guesswork never replaces the truth. So the Prophet ﷺ is told to turn away from anyone who ignores the Quran and wants only this world. That is as far as their knowledge reaches.

Everything in the heavens and earth is Allah’s, so He repays evil for evil and good with the best. The good-doers avoid major sins and shameful deeds, apart from lamam, small slips, and Allah’s forgiveness is vast. He knew you from the earth and the womb, so don’t praise yourselves: He knows who truly fears Him.
teaches: Guesswork is no basis for belief.
When this world is your only goal, it becomes the limit of your knowledge.
Avoid major sins, and trust Allah’s vast forgiveness for small slips.
Small sins become serious when you keep repeating them.
Never praise your own purity; only Allah knows who truly has taqwā.
sections.hook: Starts at the top of page 527. Huwa aʿlam, “He knows best”, comes twice in ayah 30 and twice in ayah 32. “They follow only guesswork” repeats ayah 23 in ayah 28.

sections.title: The one who stopped giving; old scriptures: no one bears another’s burden
sections.meaning: Look at the one who turned away, gave a little, then stopped. Does he see the unseen? Hasn’t he heard what is in the scriptures of Mūsā and Ibrāhīm, who fulfilled every duty? No one carries another’s sins, each gets only his own effort, and that effort will be seen and fully repaid.
points: He turned away, gave a little, then stopped: does he see the unseen?
The scriptures of Mūsā and of Ibrāhīm, who fulfilled his duty
No one bears another’s burden; each gets only what he strove for
His effort will be seen, then repaid in full
sections.matters: It shows these are not new teachings: the same rules were in the scriptures of Mūsā and Ibrāhīm. Nobody can buy a way out by having someone else carry his sins. What counts is your own effort, and all of it will be seen.
sections.story: Reportedly revealed about al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah. He leaned toward Islam, but a friend shamed him and promised to carry his punishment in the Hereafter if he paid him. He returned to idolatry, paid part, then withheld the rest. Other reports name different people.
explained: Afa-raʾayta: have you seen the one who turned away from obedience, gave a little, then akdā, stopped, like a well-digger who hits hard rock and gives up? Does he know the unseen, so he can be sure someone else will carry his punishment, or that giving will make him poor?

Hasn’t he been told what was in the scriptures of Mūsā and of Ibrāhīm, who waffā, fulfilled everything Allah commanded? No soul carries another’s burden. A person has only what he himself strove for. That effort will be shown on the Day of Judgement, then repaid in full.
teaches: Don’t start giving and then stop; Allah replaces what you spend.
No one can carry your sins for you, not even family.
Your reward comes from your own effort, so strive.
Allah sees every effort and repays it in full.
sections.hook: It opens with afa-raʾayta (33), as section 2 opened with afa-raʾaytum (19). Saʿā (39) becomes saʿyahu (40); Ibrāhīm “who fulfilled”, waffā (37), echoes al-awfā, “the fullest” (41).

sections.title: Everything returns to Allah; He gives life and wealth, and destroyed nations
sections.meaning: Everything ends with your Lord. He makes people laugh and weep, gives death and life, creates male and female from a drop, and will create again. He gives wealth, and is Lord even of Sirius. He destroyed ʿĀd, Thamūd, Nūḥ’s people and the overturned towns. So which of His favours will you doubt?
points: To your Lord is the end; He causes laughter, tears, death and life
He creates male and female from a drop, and will create again
He enriches and gives wealth to keep; He is Lord of Sirius
He destroyed ʿĀd, Thamūd, Nūḥ’s people and the overturned towns
So which of your Lord’s favours will you doubt?
sections.matters: Section 4 said every effort is repaid. This section shows the One who repays: every joy, grief, birth, death and fortune comes from Him, even the star some Arabs worshipped. The ruined nations show where denial ends, so doubt has no ground.
sections.story: No specific incident. Ayat 42–54 either continue the scriptures of Mūsā and Ibrāhīm or start a new list. Sirius is named because some Arab tribes worshipped it. The ruined nations are ʿĀd, Thamūd, Nūḥ’s people and Lūṭ’s towns.
explained: Everything returns to your Lord in the end. He creates the causes of laughter and tears, gives death and life, and makes male and female from a drop of fluid, so bringing everyone back is easy for Him. He makes people rich and gives them wealth to keep. He is Lord of Sirius, which some Arabs worshipped.

He destroyed the first ʿĀd with a violent wind, and Thamūd, sparing none. Before them He drowned Nūḥ’s people, who were even worse in wrongdoing. He lifted the towns of Lūṭ’s people, turned them upside down, and covered them with stones. After all this, which of your Lord’s favours will you doubt?
teaches: Joy and sorrow both come from Allah, not from luck or the stars.
The One who made you from a drop can easily bring you back.
Wealth is His gift, so thank Him and worship Him alone.
Nations that denied their prophets were destroyed; their fate is a warning.
sections.hook: Wa annahu, “and that He”, opens six ayat (43–45, 48–50), four with huwa. Al-muntahā (42) repeats the Lote Tree’s name (14). “Mā ghashshā” (54) mirrors “mā yaghshā” (16). Page 528 begins at 45.

sections.title: Judgement Day is near; why laugh and not weep? Prostrate to Allah
sections.meaning: This Prophet ﷺ is a warner like the warners before him. The Approaching Day has drawn near, and no one but Allah can reveal it or hold it back. Do you wonder at this message, laugh instead of weeping, and play heedlessly? So prostrate to Allah and worship Him.
points: A warner like the warners of old
The Approaching Day is near; only Allah can remove it
You wonder at this, laugh, don’t weep, and play heedlessly?
So prostrate to Allah and worship Him
sections.matters: This is the ending that reportedly overwhelmed the Quraysh: when the Prophet ﷺ recited it and prostrated, even hardened opponents fell down with him. It turns every argument in the surah into one command: bow to Allah alone.
sections.story: The Prophet ﷺ recited the surah in Makkah and prostrated at this ayah. Muslims and pagans prostrated with him, except one old man who put dust to his forehead. Al-Muṭṭalib ibn Abī Wadāʿah refused that day; after becoming Muslim he never skipped this prostration.
explained: Hādhā: this Prophet ﷺ is a warner like those sent before; he is no new kind of messenger. Al-āzifah, the Approaching Day, has come near, and no one besides Allah can reveal its time or push it away. A warner rushes to warn because the danger is close.

So do you find this Quran strange? You laugh at it, when you should weep over your sins, and you stay sāmidūn: heedless, busy with play, or, in another meaning, singing over it. Stop, and prostrate to Allah and worship Him alone, not idols.
teaches: The Prophet ﷺ brought the same message as every warner before him.
The Hour is near, and only Allah knows when it will come.
The Quran should move us to tears, not laughter or heedlessness.
Prostration is the heart of worship: bow to Allah alone.
sections.hook: The -ā rhyme that runs from ayah 1 breaks at 57 (āzifah, kāshifah), then -ūn (59–61). “You laugh and don’t weep” (60) turns ayah 43’s “He makes laugh and weep” around. Ends in sajdah.

groups.text: By the setting star: your companion hasn’t strayed or erred. He doesn’t speak from desire; it is only revelation.
A mighty, strong angel taught him, and rose in his true form on the highest horizon.
He came down within two bow-lengths or nearer, and Allah revealed to His servant what He revealed.
His heart didn’t deny what he saw. So will you argue with him about what he sees?
He saw him again at the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary, beside the Garden of Refuge.
Something indescribable covered the tree. His sight didn’t swerve or overstep, and he saw his Lord’s greatest signs.
Have you considered your idols al-Lāt, al-ʿUzzā and Manāt, the third?
Sons for you and daughters for Him? That is an unfair division.
Just names you and your fathers invented, with no proof. They follow guesswork and desire, though guidance has come.
Does man get whatever he wishes? No: the Hereafter and this life belong to Allah.
Even the angels of the heavens can intercede only after Allah permits, for someone He is pleased with.
Deniers of the Hereafter give angels female names, with no knowledge. Guesswork is no substitute for the truth.
Turn away from those who want only this world. Allah knows best who strays and who is guided.
Allah repays evil and rewards good-doers, who avoid major sins. His forgiveness is vast, so don’t claim purity.
The one who turned away, gave a little, then stopped: does he know the unseen?
Hasn’t he heard what is in the scriptures of Mūsā, and of Ibrāhīm, who fulfilled his duty?
No one bears another’s burden, and each person has only what he strove for.
His effort will be seen, and then repaid in full.
Everything ends with your Lord. He makes people laugh and weep, and He gives death and life.
He creates male and female from a drop, and He will bring about the second creation.
He makes people rich and gives them wealth to keep, and He is Lord of Sirius.
He destroyed ʿĀd and Thamūd, sparing none, and before them Nūḥ’s people, who were even worse.
He overturned Lūṭ’s towns and covered them. So which of your Lord’s favours will you doubt?
The Prophet ﷺ is a warner like those before. The Approaching Day is near, and only Allah can remove it.
Do you wonder at this message, laugh instead of weeping, and play heedlessly?
So prostrate to Allah and worship Him.

1.explain: Allah swears by an-najm as it sets: either the Pleiades at dawn or the stars in general. Stars adorn the sky and guide travellers; revelation lights and guides the earth.

2.explain: Ṣāḥibukum, “your companion”: they had known his honesty all his life. He hasn’t strayed like someone without knowledge (ḍalla), nor knowingly turned from the truth (ghawā).

3.explain: Nothing he says comes from al-hawā, his own desire. They claimed he made up the Quran himself; this ayah denies it.

4.explain: It is only waḥy, revelation sent to him, conveyed in full with nothing added or removed. This also shows his Sunnah comes from revelation.

5.explain: Shadīd al-quwā, mighty in power: Jibrīl. He is strong enough to deliver revelation safely, so no devil can snatch it or slip anything into it.

6.explain: Dhū mirrah: strong, and of fine appearance. He rose and stood in his true form, not the human form he usually came in.

7.explain: He was on al-ufuq al-aʿlā, the highest horizon in the east, where the sun rises. He reportedly filled the horizon, and the Prophet ﷺ fainted at the sight.

8.explain: Then he drew near and came down to the Prophet ﷺ to deliver revelation, reportedly now in human form, wiping the dust from his face.

9.explain: Qāba qawsayn: two bow-lengths, or even nearer. He was that close, with no one between them, so the revelation was received exactly.

10.explain: Allah revealed to His servant what He revealed, through Jibrīl. Leaving it unnamed shows how great it was. One report says it was the opening of Al-Muddaththir.

11.explain: His heart didn’t deny what his eyes saw; heart and sight agreed. Most reports say this was Jibrīl in his true form; another view says he saw his Lord with his heart.

12.explain: Afa-tumārūnahu: will you argue with him about what he sees? It addresses the pagans who denied he saw Jibrīl, like the blind arguing with someone who can see.

13.explain: He saw him again, nazlatan ukhrā, on another descent. Most reports say this was the second time he saw Jibrīl in his true form.

14.explain: Sidrat al-Muntahā: the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary, in the highest heavens. What rises from earth and what descends from above both stop there. He saw Jibrīl there on the Night Journey.

15.explain: Near it is Jannat al-Maʾwā, the Garden of Refuge: Paradise, where the angels and the souls of the righteous find shelter. It shows Paradise already exists, high above.

16.explain: Something covered the tree that only Allah can fully describe: reportedly angels, light, colours and golden butterflies.

17.explain: Mā zāgha: his sight didn’t turn right or left. Wa mā ṭaghā: it didn’t go beyond what he was allowed. Perfect manners in Allah’s presence.

18.explain: He saw some of his Lord’s greatest signs that night, like Paradise, the Fire and Jibrīl’s true form. One view takes this to mean he saw signs, not Allah Himself.

19.explain: Afa-raʾaytum: have you considered al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā? Al-Lāt was an inscribed stone at Ṭāʾif; one report says it began as the grave of a man who fed pilgrims. Al-ʿUzzā was a tree shrine at Nakhlah.

20.explain: And Manāt, the third, near Qudayd between Makkah and Madinah. Al-ukhrā, “the other”, belittles it: the lowly third. What power do any of them have?

21.explain: Alakum adh-dhakar: do you keep sons for yourselves and assign daughters to Allah, calling the angels His daughters, while hating to have daughters yourselves?
21.why: Reportedly revealed when the pagans claimed the angels, and their idols, were Allah’s daughters, while they themselves disliked having daughters.

22.explain: Qismah ḍīzā: a crooked, unjust division. It would be unfair even between people; it is far worse to rank the creature above the Creator.

23.explain: They are only names you and your forefathers invented, with no sulṭān, no proof, from Allah. They follow ẓann (guesswork) and desire, though clear guidance had come through the Prophet ﷺ.

24.explain: Does man get whatever he wishes for, such as his idols interceding for him? No. Wishing doesn’t make it so.
24.why: Reportedly about an-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith, or al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah, or the disbelievers in general, who hoped their idols would intercede for them.

25.explain: Al-ākhirah wal-ūlā: the Hereafter and this first life both belong to Allah. He gives and withholds as He wills, not as people wish.

26.explain: Even the many honoured angels can’t intercede unless two conditions meet: Allah permits it, and He is pleased with the one they speak for. So what can idols do?

27.explain: Because they don’t believe in the Hereafter, they dare to give the angels female names, calling them Allah’s daughters.

28.explain: They have no knowledge of this, only ẓann, guesswork, and guesswork is no substitute for the truth. This means baseless guessing, not careful judgement built on evidence.

29.explain: Turn away from whoever ignores Our reminder, the Quran, and wants only this worldly life. This came before fighting was permitted.
29.why: Reportedly revealed about an-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith, or about al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah.

30.explain: Mablaghuhum min al-ʿilm: this world is the limit of their knowledge. Your Lord knows best who strays from His path and who is guided, and will repay both.

31.explain: Everything in the heavens and earth belongs to Allah, so He repays those who do evil for what they did, and rewards those who do good with al-ḥusnā, the best: Paradise.

32.explain: Good-doers avoid major sins and shameful deeds, except lamam: small slips, or a sin done once then repented. Allah’s forgiveness is vast. He knew you from creation and in the womb, so don’t praise yourselves.
32.why: Reportedly revealed about people who boasted of “our prayer, our fasting, our Hajj”. Other reports link it to a man who regretted a near-sin, to sins from before Islam, or to a claim that a child who died young was surely righteous.

33.explain: Afa-raʾayta: have you seen the one who tawallā, who turned away from faith and obedience?
33.why: Reportedly al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah. He leaned toward Islam; a friend who shamed him promised to carry his punishment for a payment. He returned to idolatry, paid part and withheld the rest. Other reports name different people.

34.explain: He gave a little, then akdā: stopped, like a well-digger who hits hard rock and can dig no further. Either he paid part of a promised sum, or gave charity briefly, then quit.

35.explain: Does he know the unseen, so he can see that someone else will bear his punishment, or that giving will leave him poor? He knows neither.

36.explain: Or hasn’t he been told what is in the ṣuḥuf, the scriptures, of Mūsā: the Torah, or scrolls given before it?

37.explain: …and of Ibrāhīm, alladhī waffā: who fulfilled everything Allah commanded him, passed his tests and delivered the message in full.

38.explain: No soul carries another’s burden of sin, not even a relative’s. It cancels any promise to carry someone else’s punishment.

39.explain: A person has only what he himself strove for; no one can fulfil another’s duties for him. Ongoing charity, useful knowledge and a righteous child still count as his own effort. Most allow gifting others the reward of voluntary deeds.

40.explain: Sawfa yurā: his effort will be seen on the Day of Judgement, weighed for its sincerity, not just its outward form.

41.explain: Then he is repaid al-jazāʾ al-awfā, the fullest repayment: good for good and evil for evil, so justly that all creation praises Allah for it.

42.explain: Al-muntahā: all creation returns to your Lord in the end, for judgement. It can also mean human thinking reaches its limit at Him: reflect on His creation, not His essence.

43.explain: He makes people laugh and weep: He creates joy and sorrow and their causes. Causes don’t act on their own; He can turn laughter to tears at any moment.

44.explain: He causes death in this world and gives life again at the resurrection. He alone creates life and ends it.

45.explain: He creates the two kinds, male and female, in people and animals alike.

46.explain: …from a nuṭfah, a drop, when it is emitted into the womb. From something so weak He builds a whole person.

47.explain: An-nashʾah al-ukhrā: the second creation is upon Him. The One who began creation will bring it back for the Resurrection.

48.explain: Aghnā wa aqnā: He makes people rich and gives them wealth to keep and store. Another meaning: He gives, then makes them content.

49.explain: He is Lord of ash-Shiʿrā, Sirius, the bright star some Arab tribes worshipped. Even what they worshipped is created and ruled by Him.

50.explain: He destroyed ʿĀd al-ūlā, the first ʿĀd, Hūd’s people, among the strongest nations, with a furious wind.

51.explain: …and Thamūd, Ṣāliḥ’s people, who killed the she-camel sent as a sign. A mighty blast destroyed them, and He spared none.

52.explain: …and Nūḥ’s people before them, who were even more unjust and rebellious: Nūḥ called them for 950 years and they harmed him. They were drowned.

53.explain: Al-muʾtafikah: the overturned towns of Lūṭ’s people. They were lifted up, then hurled down upside down.

54.explain: Then they were covered by what covered them: a rain of stones of baked clay. Leaving it unnamed makes it more terrifying.

55.explain: Fa-bi-ayyi ālāʾi rabbika tatamārā: which of your Lord’s favours, O man, will you doubt? Every blessing is from Him, and even this warning is a favour.

56.explain: Hādhā: this Prophet ﷺ, or this Quran, is a warning like the warners of old. He is not a new kind of messenger.

57.explain: Azifat al-āzifah: the Approaching Day has approached. The Hour has drawn near, and its signs have appeared.

58.explain: No one besides Allah can remove it, hold it back, or reveal its time.

59.explain: Do you wonder at this ḥadīth, this Quran, treating it as strange and false?

60.explain: …and laugh at it mockingly, and not weep, as believers weep when they hear its warnings?

61.explain: Sāmidūn: heedless and busy with play. It can also mean singing: they reportedly sang and played when they heard the Quran.

62.explain: So prostrate to Allah and worship Him alone, not idols. Prostration is the heart of worship: the forehead, a person’s most honoured part, goes to the ground. Views differ on whether this prostration is obligatory.
